This procession of ours is for the image of Vishnu, by Keshava's command; whatever is to be done for Vishnu, may that be so for you too.
agnipuran:43:21	Be pleased in every way by this gift of offering.
Awakened, the beings go, satisfied, as they please. The sculptors, having eaten the porridge, should recite the dream-mantra at night:

Om, homage to the lord of all worlds, Vishnu, the powerful, the universe, of universal form, lord of dreams, homage.
agnipuran:43:24	Tell me, lord of the gods of gods; I lie asleep near you; in dream all those matters that are in my heart.
agnipuran:43:25	Om Om Hrum phat, to Vishnu, svaha. In a good dream all is good; in a bad one, by the Simha oblation. In the morning, having given arghya on the stone, one should worship the weapon with the weapon-mantra,
the spade, chisel and the like, smeared on the mouth with honey. One should contemplate oneself as Vishnu, the sculptor Vishvakarman;
one should give the weapon made of Vishnu, and show the face and back and so on. The sculptor, self-controlled, chisel in hand, having made the stone square,
should arrange it a little less for the pedestal. Having set it in a cart and brought it with cloth to the craftsman's house, having worshipped, the maker should shape the image.
By breadth the palm is declared six fingers; the length should be seven fingers; the middle finger is held at five.
The index and ring fingers half a finger less than that; the little finger and thumb should be four fingers.
The thumb should have two joints; the other fingers three joints; the nail is prescribed as half the joint of each.
The belly is proportioned by the measure of the chest. The navel is one finger by the piercing and by measure.
Then the interval to the organ should be a span in measure; at the middle of the navel the girth is forty-two fingers.
The interval of the breasts should be a span; the chin barley-sized; the circle two feet.
The girth of the chest should be sixty-four fingers, evident; the girth below that is declared four-faced.
The girth at the hip likewise is fifty-four fingers; the breadth at the root of the thigh is said to be twelve fingers.
More than that in the middle, then narrower in order; the knee eight fingers wide, its girth three times.
The breadth in the middle of the shank is declared seven fingers; its girth three times; the end of the shank five by breadth.
Its girth three times; the feet a span; rising from the length, the feet four fingers.
Before the ankle four fingers by measure; the feet three-part wide; the heel is remembered as three fingers.
Its girth five fingers, the forefinger likewise long; the remaining fingers in order less by an eighth part.
The height of the thumb is declared a finger and a quarter; the finger less a barley, and likewise the thumb-nail.
Half a finger, and the others in order less; the testes a finger; the organ four fingers.
Its girth and the tip of the sheath should be four fingers; the testes are declared six fingers in girth.
The image should be rich in ornaments; this is the indicated mark; in this manner one should make it, seeing the marks in the world.
In the right hand the discus with the lotus below; in the left the conch with the mace below, from the mark of Vasudeva.
Shri and Pushti should be made, with lotus and lute in hand, of thigh height; Mala and Vidyadhara likewise,
standing in the halo, with the halo adorned with elephants and the like. A lotus-like footstool one should make for images thus.
The eyes should be long, three barleys less a third; for half of that one should arrange the breadth of the eyes.
The ear-lobe should be longer, equal to the line from the corner of the mouth; bent, lacking a part, make two parts likewise.
The neck should be a part and a half, adorned with its breadth. Except for the eye, the breadths, thighs, knees and calves,
back of the feet, buttocks and hips, one should arrange according to proportion. The fingers less by a seventh; the length multiplied by the breadth,
the shanks, thighs and hip with length less one eye; its middle and side round, dense and full: the two breasts.
The breasts should be a span; the hip a part and a half more. The remaining marks as before; in the right hand a lotus,
in the left a fruit; two women at the sides, auspicious, with fly-whisks in hand. Garuda with a long nose; now I shall tell of the discus and other marks.
Ananta with a serpent-coil body, of many lights, of many forms; Damodara stout; middle-wheeled; the door-guard with a fine dot.
Sudarshana with one wheel; Lakshmi-Narayana with two; Achyuta, the god, with three wheels; or Trivikrama with three wheels.
Janardana with four wheels; Vasudeva with five; Pradyumna with six; Sankarshana with seven;
Purushottama with eight wheels; the nine-fold array marked with nine; the Ten Avatars with ten; Aniruddha with eleven; of twelve natures with twelve; above that, Anantaka.
One should worship the Creator, the Doer and the Taker in the south and north, Vishvaksena in the northeast, the field-guardian in the southeast.
In the east and elsewhere the Vedas beginning with the Rik, the support Ananta, the earth, the seat, the lotus, and the three orbs called sun, moon and fire.
Having placed the seat with the twelve-syllable mantra, one should worship the stone there. One should worship in order with separate and combined seed-syllables.
In the east and elsewhere, with the Vedas and others, with the two Gayatris, the Jita and the rest, one should worship with Om; afterward one should show three mudras.
One should show those of Vishvaksena, of the discus, and of the field-guardian. The first worship of the Shalagrama is said to be for purposes that are fruitless.
As before one should draw a mandala with sixteen spokes and a lotus; with conch, discus, mace and sword one should worship the teacher and others as before.
In the east and north, bow and arrows; one should give the seat with the Vedas and the rest; one should place the stone with the twelve-syllable mantra; hear the third worship.

One should draw an eight-spoked lotus and worship the teacher and others as before; having given the seat with the eight-syllable mantra and placing the stone with that, one should worship it tenfold with that, likewise the Jita with the two Gayatris.
Discus, sword, pestle and goad in the left hand; conch, Sharnga, mace and noose, with lotus and lute —
Lakshmi and Sarasvati are to be made; then the universal form on the right: mace, noose, spear, trident and arrow in the hand;
on the left conch, Sharnga, mace, noose and spear; plow, axe, staff, knife, shield and sling —
twenty-armed, four-faced, standing at the right and the left; three-eyed, on the left side; not lying, though water-lying.
With one foot held by Shri, praised by Vimala and others; the four-faced one on the navel-lotus; Hari-Shankara, Hari,
holding trident and spear on the right, mace and discus in the foot; marked with Rudra and Keshava in his body, with Gauri and Lakshmi;
hands with conch, discus, mace and Veda; Hari with horse's head. The left foot is held on Shesha, the right on the tortoise's back.
Dattatreya should be two-armed, with Shri on his left lap. Vishvaksena with discus and mace, plow and conch is Hari's attendant.
On the right, hands with fruit-offering — Saubhagya — and above her; Lakshmi with right hand a lotus, on the left holding a shri-fruit;
Sarasvati with book and rosary in hand and lute in hand; Jahnavi (Ganga), fair-hued, with pot and lotus in hand, on a crocodile;
Yamuna on a tortoise, with pot in hand, dark, is worshipped. Tumburu with lute, white, with trident, in front of the mothers on a bull;
Gauri; four-faced Brahmi with rosary and... ; on the left with a pot and bowl, riding a swan, white Shankari;
arrow and bow on her right, on the left a discus and bow, on a bull. Kaumari on a peacock, red, with spear in hand, two-armed;
on the right holding discus and conch, on the left Lakshmi holding mace and lotus; Varahi on a buffalo with staff, conch, sword and mace;
Aindri on the left with thunderbolt in hand, thousand-eyed, for accomplishment. Chamunda is Kotaraghni, fleshless, three-eyed,
fleshless or bone-essence, with upward hair and thin belly; wearing a tiger skin; on the left a skull and a spear in her hand;
trident and knife on her right; mounted on a corpse, adorned with bones. Vinayaka is human-formed, with large belly and elephant face,
large trunk, with the sacred thread; the face is seven parts. By breadth and length the trunk is thirty-six fingers.
The vein is twelve parts; the neck rises a part and a half; the throat thirty-six fingers; the secret part a finger and a half;
the navel and thighs twelve; shanks and feet on the right. His own tusk and axe in the left; a sweet ball and lotus lying.
With good face and cat-like eyes; at his side Skanda on a peacock; Svami, Shakha, Vishakha, two-armed, bearing a child's form,
on the right spear, and a cock; one-faced or six-faced; six-armed or twelve-armed; in village or forest two-armed;
with spear, arrows, noose, sword, goad and threatening finger; with spear in six right hands, and likewise in the left hand,
peacock feather, bow, shield, banner, fearlessness, and a cock; holding skull, knife, trident and noose in the south and north;
bearing an elephant hide, with face and feet upward, is Rudra-Charchika. The same goddess eight-armed, with head and drum,
is thus Rudra-Chamunda, or Nateshvari dancing. This same Mahalakshmi seated, four-faced,
eating men, horses, buffaloes and elephants held in her hand; ten-armed and three-eyed, with weapon, sword, and drum, three —
